title: Hazel and the Hollow
premise: Wendell Brightwater has spent thirty years as the invisible keeper of the Hollow Gate, keeping ledgers for a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed years, names not yet earned. When a child named Hazel arrives at his door speaking a language that predates kingdoms, he learns she is the last heir of Vessany, a country erased from maps and memory, and that the guild itself engineered its erasure. To save her, Wendell must reopen a door out of a nation that no longer exists, betraying the guild that sheltered him and gathering a found family of smugglers, exiles, and one reformed assassin. In the end, Wendell sacrifices his own recorded name—the guild's claim on his existence—to carry Hazel through the door into restored Vessany, choosing justice outside any law over the safety of being forgotten.
about_author: Hazel Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the paperwork of defunct institutions and now writes fantasy about what those papers were hiding. They live near a border town that has changed countries four times without moving an inch.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A quiet night of bookkeeping at the Hollow Gate establishes the guild's trade in impossible things and Wendell's careful invisibility. He balances accounts for bottled grief and borrowed years. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine, shadowed by loneliness—he hasn't spoken his own name aloud in years.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Old Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A mud-streaked child arrives at the gate speaking a language no living kingdom remembers, asking for 'the door home.' Wendell recognizes the tongue from the oldest ledger, one written before the guild existed. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant wonder; his invisibility is ending whether he likes it or not.

chapters.title: What the Guild Erased
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Researching the child's words, Wendell finds pages razored from the founding ledgers and a map with a country-shaped hole labeled only 'Vessany.' The child, Hazel, draws the missing borders from memory. Emotional beat: quiet horror as Wendell realizes the guild didn't just trade in impossibilities—it manufactured one.

chapters.title: The Toll Collector's Daughter
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Through Hazel's eyes we see her flight from the salt flats where her village was 'unwritten,' and her grandmother's dying instruction to find the keeper of the gate. She doesn't trust Wendell, but he smells like ink and old promises. Emotional beat: grief braided with stubborn hope; she has come too far to be turned away.

chapters.title: Auditors
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The guild sends Auditors to inspect the Gate after rumors of an unwritten child. Wendell hides Hazel inside a ledger-entry—a trick that costs him three years of his own recorded life. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve; for the first time, Wendell lies to the guild on purpose.

chapters.title: The Smuggler Who Owes Everyone
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell seeks out Brannoc Vale, a disgraced guild courier who once moved cargo through doors that shouldn't open. Brannoc owes debts to everyone except, conveniently, Wendell. Emotional beat: wary comedy giving way to something like loyalty; Brannoc agrees because Hazel speaks the language of his own vanished hometown.

chapters.title: Nine Names for One Door
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The trio deciphers the founding ledger: the door out of Vessany has nine locks, each keyed to a name the guild stole when it erased the country. Hazel can pronounce them; she cannot yet remember them. Emotional beat: frustration and small triumphs as the child becomes the expedition's indispensable heart.

chapters.title: The Market of Unclaimed Things
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. To buy passage through the Underways, they visit a black market where erasure victims' belongings are sold. Wendell finds a coat with his mother's buttons—proof he too was written out of somewhere. Emotional beat: vertigo and tenderness; Wendell realizes Hazel's story is also his own.

chapters.title: An Assassin Changes Sides
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The guild sends Serevan, its best knife, to retrieve the child. Instead of killing them, she reads Hazel's handwriting in the old tongue and goes pale—her own name is among the nine stolen ones. Emotional beat: betrayal turned inward; Serevan joins the company with a blade still wet from her last obedience.

chapters.title: The Underways
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The company descends beneath the borderlands, where geography forgets itself. They pass ruins wearing Vessany's architecture like a bad disguise. An Auditor patrol nearly corners them; Brannoc holds a collapsing bridge so the others escape. Emotional beat: sacrifice and rising stakes—the guild knows exactly where they are.

chapters.title: What Brannoc Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Brannoc (via Wendell's narration). Around a fire, Brannoc confesses he was the courier who carried the final decree of erasure out of Vessany, believing it was grain manifests. His guilt explains his debts—and his fury. Emotional beat: confession as absolution; the found family binds itself with shared guilt rather than shared blood.

chapters.title: The First Lock
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. At the drowned tollhouse, Hazel speaks the first stolen name and the lock answers—but each name spoken costs the speaker a memory of Vessany. She gives up her memory of her grandmother's face. Emotional beat: bittersweet courage; the way home must be paid for with the home itself.

chapters.title: Ledger-Bound
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The guild, unable to find them physically, attacks contractually: it invokes clauses proving Wendell's name belongs to the ledgers, meaning his body and choices do too. He stalls the summons by filing a countersuit in the guild's own archaic legal language. Emotional beat: defiant cleverness; justice outside the law begins with mastering the law's grammar.

chapters.title: Serevan's Name
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. At the second lock, Serevan discovers her stolen name is her own—that the guild made her by erasing her. Speaking it at the lock would free her but unmake her training, her loyalties, her self. She speaks it anyway. Emotional beat: rebirth through loss; the second lock opens and Serevan weeps without knowing why.

chapters.title: The Archive That Dreams
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The remaining names are held in the Living Archive, a vault where erased records dream their lost contents. To retrieve them, Wendell must enter the dream and confront the ledger-ghost of the guild's founder, who offers him restoration of everything he's sacrificed—in exchange for Hazel. Emotional beat: temptation met with clarity; Wendell refuses for the first time in thirty years.

chapters.title: Riot of the Unwritten
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Escaping the Archive, they release its dreaming contents, and the erased people of Vessany briefly walk again in the streets above—long enough to remember, and to rise. The city burns with lanterns and demands. Emotional beat: furious joy; justice arrives not as verdict but as uprising.

chapters.title: The Founder's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Cornered by the guild's full council, Wendell argues Vessany's case using their own ledgers against them: the erasure was filed illegally, witnessed by the founder's own hand. The council fractures. Emotional beat: triumph undercut by cost—the council grants a hearing but seizes Brannoc as collateral.

chapters.title: Seven Locks, No Time
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Racing to the door with Auditors behind them, the company spends names and memories in desperate succession. Brannoc gives his memory of the road home; Wendell gives his of the guild that raised him. Emotional beat: breathless momentum; every step forward is something beloved left behind.

chapters.title: The Last Name
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The ninth lock requires the name of the one who kept the gate—the role Wendell has hidden inside for thirty years. He realizes the guild never knew his true name because he gave it away long ago to protect someone. The name was Hazel's grandmother's to keep, and she passed it to the child. Emotional beat: revelation; the keeper and the key were always the same family.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Vessany
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. At the threshold, the door will open only if a recorded name is surrendered to seal it behind them. Wendell strikes his own name from the guild's master ledger—unmaking their claim, his history, his protection. The door opens onto green hills that have waited thirty years. Emotional beat: awe and heartbreak entwined; freedom purchased with oblivion.

chapters.title: A Country That Remembers Itself
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Vessany reknits around its returning heir: borders redrawn, bells rung in the old tongue, the unwritten called back by name. Hazel, now custodian of both nations' memories, begins writing a new kind of ledger—one that records gifts, not debts. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into stewardship; inheritance means keeping, not owning.

chapters.title: The Keeper Without a Name
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Nameless but not gone, Wendell stays in Vessany as the new gate's keeper, remembered only by the people he chose—Brannoc, Serevan, and Hazel, who writes his story into her ledger so he exists somewhere better than a guild's books. Emotional beat: quiet peace; found family as the one record no institution can erase.
